clue.text: Bent on making extravagant 'statements ?

parts.note: reads as someone intent on exaggeration, but describes the bent weapon of the archer, whose drawing is the idiom for telling tall tales

explanation.surface: Someone is determined to keep making wild claims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To draw the long bow' is an old idiom meaning to exaggerate; the bow itself is a bent weapon, so 'Bent' points at the object as well as the attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The archer's big yew weapon is bent when strung, and drawing one is the idiom for exaggerating.

clue.text: Pour out wine for one table as arranged

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding pieces are set out in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Serving drinks to each guest as the table is laid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as arranged' rearranges I and TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a ritual offering of a drink by spilling it is the verb meaning to pour out wine.

clue.text: Smarter painter

explanation.surface: A more stylish artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Marc Nattier was an eighteenth-century French portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means neat and dapper, so its comparative means smarter; Nattier is also a French rococo portraitist.

clue.text: Speedy way to open a bottle

explanation.surface: Advice on the fastest method of uncorking.
explanation.walkthrough: One way to open a bottle is to break its neck off.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangerously fast describes speed, and snapping off the bottle's top describes a rough uncorking.

clue.text: A victory for those who "box the compass"?

definitions.text: A victory for those who "box the compass"?

parts.words: A victory for those who "box the compass"?
parts.note: a boxer's victory decided by the judges' scores, joined to the compass points that sailors recite

explanation.surface: A triumph for sailors who can recite their bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'box the compass' is to recite all 32 compass points in order; a boxing match not ended by a knockout is decided on points.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing bout decided by the judges' scorecards rather than a knockout ends this way.

clue.text: Drawing an unloaded vehicle ?

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle
with nothing on it: O (nothing) followed by ON

explanation.surface: Someone sketches an empty wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: An unloaded cart has nothing (O) on it, so after CART comes O and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic sketch or preparatory sketch for a painting is a kind of drawing.

clue.text: Tom follows a tip for the game.

definitions.text: follows a tip for the game.

explanation.surface: A tomcat trails after a tip about a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip-cat is an old children's game in which a short tapered stick is tipped up and struck, so this word follows TIP to name the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom is a male of the feline species, and tip-cat is a traditional stick game.

clue.text: It's the right page

parts.note: reads as finding the correct place in a book, but describes which side of an open volume a leaf faces

explanation.surface: Someone confirms the page they have found is the correct one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' reads as correct, but means right-hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers call the right-hand page of an open book, the front of a leaf, by this Latin term.

clue.text: Duck part of the big speech ?

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so O
a ration is a share or portion

explanation.surface: A duck takes its share of a long talk.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal public address on a grand occasion is a big speech.

clue.text: Appoint many in Etonian disguise

indicators.note: in disguise, letters appear in a changed form

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: Choosing a crowd of public schoolboys in fancy dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguise' rearranges M and ETONIAN; an Etonian is a pupil of Eton, an English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward or name someone for a post is to appoint them.

clue.text: Flatter Colonel Gilbert, growing up in N America ?

parts.note: to butter someone up is to flatter them
'Gilbert the Filbert, the Colonel of the Knuts' was a music-hall song, a knut or nut being an Edwardian dandy

explanation.surface: A tale of sweet-talking an officer while he was being raised in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert the Filbert is the hero of a 1914 British music-hall song, styled 'Colonel of the Knuts', a knut (nut) being a young man-about-town.
explanation.definitionFit: The white walnut tree is native to eastern North America and grows wild there.

clue.text: One of music's magic attributes, they say

definitions.text: One of music's magic attributes, they say

parts.words: One of music's magic attributes, they say
parts.note: points to the saying that music has the power to soothe a savage breast

explanation.surface: A remark about music's supposed powers.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'Music has charms to soothe a savage breast', from Congreve, so 'they say' marks the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A magical spell or enchanting quality is what the proverb credits music with.

clue.text: Tank of considerable import

parts.note: a tank that matters is the policy group named with this word before it

explanation.surface: A heavy military vehicle of real significance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tank' suggests armour or water storage, but the clue wants the word that goes in front of it in the name for an expert policy body.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy institute is called a ___ tank, a body whose ideas carry weight.

clue.text: Patriarchal senator in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble, the letters of the preceding words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A fatherly legislator gets into difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges SENATOR and IN. Nestorius was a fifth-century Patriarch of Constantinople.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to Nestorius, the Constantinople patriarch whose teaching founded a church.

clue.text: Tender, but crooked girl

parts.note: one who tends a flock, carrying a crook, rather than a dishonest young woman

explanation.surface: A gentle young woman who is nonetheless dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' is one who tends, and 'crooked' means carrying a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who tends sheep carries a shepherd's crook.

clue.text: A smooth tie ? Of course not

definitions.text: A smooth tie ? Of course not

parts.words: A smooth tie ? Of course not
parts.note: a tie between sweethearts, with 'Of course' giving true and 'not' sounding like the knot

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a tie is sleek and is told firmly no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' is TRUE and 'not' plays on KNOT; the whole is the ornamental bow of interlaced loops that symbolises lovers' fidelity.
explanation.definitionFit: This ornamental double bow of interlaced loops is a traditional emblem of faithful romance.

clue.text: Drawing pipe through a broken sieve

indicators.note: one piece runs through the middle of the other
a broken thing is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: a duct is a pipe or channel

explanation.surface: Pulling a tube through a damaged strainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the strainer's letters and 'through' sets the pipe inside them; 'Drawing' means attractive, not sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alluring draws a person in, so it is attractive or tempting.

clue.text: Where all goes swimmingly, tanked up with water, one in three parts spirit

definitions.text: Where all goes swimmingly, tanked up

parts.note: aqua is Latin for water

indicators.note: one piece put inside the other

parts.note: rum is a spirit of three letters
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A boozy picture: everything going well once someone is full of water and spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the numeral inside the spirit; 'tanked up' sounds like drunk but points to the fish tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass tank where fish swim is somewhere everything moves through water.

clue.text: Prompt in response as a 27 or a 5 ac artist might be

definitions.text: as a 27 or a 5 ac artist might be

explanation.surface: Describing a quick reply, and the sort of person who draws a gun or a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The 27 is SHERIFF, who draws a gun, and the 5 across is CARTOON, whose artist draws pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means fast to react, and literally fits a gunslinging lawman or a fast-sketching illustrator.

clue.text: Fix public relations in one money-making concern

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the mint is where money is literally made

explanation.surface: Sorting out the publicity for a profitable business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the publicity abbreviation inside the money-maker, after the numeral; the commas in the newspaper text are misprints.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp or impress a mark firmly on something is to fix it there.

clue.text: Help, aid rebuilding of Adam's London

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the letters of the words together in a new structure

explanation.surface: A plea for help with reconstructing a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilding of' rearranges HELP and AID. The Adelphi was a London riverside development by the Adam brothers, Scottish architects.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adam brothers designed this Strand terrace development in eighteenth-century London.

clue.text: Of this, part is where offices are planned

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A remark about an area zoned for office buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' takes a run of letters from 'wHERE OFfices'.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal legal word meaning concerning the thing just mentioned.

clue.text: Valuer who commends a piano ?

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
one who commends is a praiser

explanation.surface: An assessor speaks well of a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who estimates the worth of goods professionally is a valuer.

clue.text: Protected, having broken one's dream

indicators.note: broken means the word dream is shattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone stays safe but their dream has been shattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges DREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying weapons means being equipped for defence.

clue.text: Where Miss Lloyd was once stationed in error

definitions.text: Where Miss Lloyd was once stationed in error

parts.words: Where Miss Lloyd was once stationed in error
parts.note: recalls the music-hall song in which Marie Lloyd's train takes her to the wrong station

explanation.surface: A singer ended up at the wrong stop.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Lloyd sang 'Oh! Mr Porter', whose singer wanted Birmingham but was taken on to this railway junction town in Cheshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cheshire town is a major railway junction, the wrong stop in the old music-hall song.

clue.text: Man follows primitive instincts. Say, that's peculiar

indicators.note: one piece coming after another, so the island goes second

parts.note: in Freud, the id is the mind's store of primitive instincts
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Someone notices a man acting on base urges and remarks on how odd it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' puts the island after the Freudian term; 'Say' introduces the definition, an expression peculiar to a language.
explanation.definitionFit: An expression particular to one language, whose sense is not the sum of its words, is a saying peculiar to it.

clue.text: Pay Peter his charge, but no, rent for it

definitions.text: Pay Peter his charge, but no, rent for it

parts.words: Pay Peter his charge, but no, rent for it
parts.note: a payment or charge, but land held outright on which no rent is due

explanation.surface: Settling a bill but owing no rent.
explanation.walkthrough: A fee is a charge, and in English law land held in fee simple is owned outright, with no rent owed to any lord.
explanation.definitionFit: In property law it is absolute freehold ownership, so the holder pays nobody rent.

clue.text: Where promising youths or marathon runners should go

definitions.text: Where promising youths or marathon runners should go

parts.words: Where promising youths or marathon runners should go
parts.note: the idiom for a youngster with a bright future, taken literally for long-distance runners

explanation.surface: A note on the destiny of talented young people and long-distance athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: A promising youngster is said to be going to 'go far', which a marathon runner does literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for great success in life also describes covering a long distance.

clue.text: Bull-fighter's quite a card

explanation.surface: Praise for a toreador who is quite a character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite a card' sounds like a character, but in the card games ombre and quadrille, and in dominoes, the matadors are the top trumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A toreador who kills the bull in the ring, and a top trump in the old card game ombre.

clue.text: Star performer in Westerns

parts.note: not a leading actor but the lawman who wears a star-shaped badge in cowboy films

explanation.surface: The lead actor of cowboy films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity actor, but it is the badge on the lawman's chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The county lawman of a cowboy film wears a star-shaped badge.
